description:
Oyster Plant (Tradescantia spathacea), also known as Moses-in-the-Cradle, is a houseplant with vivid purple and green leaves. The ASPCA lists Tradescantia as toxic to cats, with dermatitis (skin irritation) as the documented clinical sign. Its sap acts as a contact irritant.

If a broken leaf oozes sap onto a cat's skin or fur, it can cause localized redness, itching, or a rash. Chewing the plant may also cause mild mouth or stomach upset in some cats, though skin irritation from sap contact is the harm confirmed by authorities.

Because of its colorful leaves, the oyster plant can attract curious cats. It is best to keep it out of reach. If your cat gets sap on its skin, wash the area gently with water to prevent a rash. Contact a veterinarian if your cat eats the plant and any drooling or stomach upset does not improve.
name: Oyster Plant
safetyNotes: Toxic principle: the sap contains an unidentified irritant; the ASPCA does not list calcium oxalate for this plant
Mechanism: sap contact causes contact dermatitis (skin irritation), the clinical sign documented by the ASPCA
Symptoms: skin or eye contact with sap may cause redness, irritation, or rash; some cats may also drool or vomit after chewing the plant
The ornamental purple-and-green leaves make this a popular houseplant — keep it out of cat reach
Symptoms are usually mild; rinse any sap off skin with water and consult your vet if GI symptoms persist

treatments.description: Gently wipe out the cat's mouth and thoroughly clean its paws to remove any remaining toxic, irritant sap
treatments.name: Oral and Paw Decontamination
treatments.notes: This is an urgent at-home first aid step to stop the sap from causing further irritation to the skin or gastrointestinal tract1. Because the plant's toxicity is mild, this is often the only intervention required. 2. Observation and Monitoring

treatments.description: Keep a close eye on the cat for a period of time after exposure, watching for signs of mild gastrointestinal upset (drooling or vomiting) or skin redness/rash
treatments.name: Symptomatic Monitoring
treatments.notes: If the vomiting is persistent, or if the skin rash worsens and does not resolve on its own, it is time to consult a veterinarian for professional guidance. 3. Veterinary Symptomatic Support (If Symptoms Worsen)

treatments.description: If the cat's symptoms escalate, a veterinarian will assess the animal and provide targeted medical relief, which may include anti-emetic medications to stop persistent vomiting or treatments to soothe severe skin irritation.
treatments.name: Veterinary Symptomatic Care
treatments.notes: Because Oyster Plant ingestion typically only results in mild, self-limiting symptoms, this step is only necessary for cats that have an unusually severe reaction or do not recover quickly
